===============================================================================
RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Technical Installations and Ancillary Charges Edition
Fictional mock document created for test purposes only. All wording is
invented. No real contract.
===============================================================================

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, and further natural hazards among them. Which of the
insurable perils are actually covered is agreed between insurer and policyholder
and recorded in the schedule.

Where an insured building, or a technical installation forming part of it, is
destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies the cost of putting it back. The
normal arrangement is reinstatement in the same kind and quality, to a condition
as new, on an index-linked reinstatement basis with an enhancement. What the
insurer carries is the restoration of what the insured event destroyed or
damaged, at the standard that was in place before it, by the ordinary means. It
is not a contribution towards the equipment, the capacity, the appearance or the
convenience of the building beyond that, and it does not become one because the
further work is carried out on the same occasion, in the same room or under the
same commission.

A limited and exhaustively listed range of consequential expenses triggered by a
loss event - debris removal and demolition among them - is also carried.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover
calculable. They appear in three places in these conditions: as general
exclusions applying across the contract, within the provisions on individual
perils and types of damage, and within the description of the insured property.

Affected item - an installation, a component, a surface or a room in which
physical damage caused by the insured event is established by the loss
investigation. Whether an item is an affected item turns on whether the event
damaged it. It does not turn on which room the item serves, on where in that
room it sits, on what it stands near, or on whether other items in the same room
were damaged.

Firmly connected - joined to the fabric of the building in such a way that
removing the item requires work on that fabric. An item that can be taken from
one place to another, set down elsewhere and used there without such work is not
firmly connected, whatever its size, price or designation, and whether or not it
is delivered together with fixed elements.

Like-for-like replacement - an item taking the place of an affected item that
can no longer be repaired, corresponding to it in type, quality, grade, output,
capacity, function and specification.

New equipment - an appliance, a plant item, a machine or a technical
installation supplied after the insured event that is not a like-for-like
replacement of an affected item. An item that was in the building but that the
event did not damage counts as new equipment for these purposes if it is
renewed, upgraded or supplemented.

Ancillary charge - a charge that exists only because of a principal item of
supply or work: its transport, forwarding, freight, carriage, delivery,
packaging, handling, lifting, hoisting and storage; the labour of putting it in
place, connecting it and commissioning it; and the attendance of the undertaking
at the building.

Index-linked reinstatement cover with enhancement - a basis of cover that works
from the amount that would have to be spent to rebuild in the same kind and
quality. Any additional cost caused by public-law restrictions on reinstatement
is picked up automatically. In addition, the level of cover is tracked against
movements in building costs; that tracking affects both the amount payable and
the premium.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before,
during and after an insured event. Observing safety requirements against fire or
frost is an example. Breaching a duty puts the cover at risk.

Secured lenders - creditors whose claim is secured by a charge registered
against the property. Their interests enjoy statutory protection: among other
things they must be brought into the process when insurance benefits are paid
out and when the contract is brought to an end.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or
lost as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the three groups (a), (b) and (c1) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1); they are not available on a standalone basis.

2.3 The fire group defined

2.3.1 Fire
A fire is a combustion that has started without a hearth intended for it, or
that has escaped such a hearth, and that is capable of spreading under its own
power. Damage caused by a fire that developed out of a controlled, purposeful
fire is also covered.

2.3.2 Lightning strike
The direct passage of a lightning discharge onto property.

2.3.3 Overvoltage caused by lightning
Damage arising through overvoltage, overcurrent or short circuit, brought about
by a lightning discharge or by other atmospheric electricity, in insured
electrical installations and appliances.

Where such an event damages several insured installations, each of them is an
affected item and each is indemnified on its own merits, whether they serve the
same room or different rooms of the building. Conversely, an installation that
the event did not damage is not brought within the indemnity by the fact that a
neighbouring installation was damaged.

2.3.4 Explosion and deflagration
Both are suddenly running force events resting on the tendency of gases or
vapours to expand. The two differ only in the intensity of that force.

An explosion of a vessel - a boiler, a pipe run and the like - is present only
under a further condition: the vessel wall must be torn open to such an extent
that a sudden equalisation of the pressure difference between the inside and
the outside occurs. Where an explosion inside a vessel is brought about by a
chemical reaction, tearing of the wall is not required.

2.3.5 Implosion
A sudden, unforeseen collapse of a hollow body under external overpressure
resulting from an internal underpressure.

2.3.6 Impact or crash of an aircraft
The impact or crash of an aircraft is covered, and equally the impact or crash
of its parts or its cargo.

2.3.7 Vehicle impact
The impact of a road, rail or water-borne vehicle against insured property is
covered, as is the impact of parts or cargo of such a vehicle. Consequential
damage to insured property arising from such an impact is covered.

Not covered is damage caused by a road or water-borne vehicle whose keeper or
driver is the policyholder or an occupant of the building.

Not covered is damage to vehicles, to their parts and cargo, and to roads,
drives and comparable trafficked surfaces.

2.3.8 Scorching
Scorch damage arising out of one of the events in 2.3.1 to 2.3.7 is covered.
Scorch damage from any other cause is covered up to [amount].

2.3.9 Smoke and soot
Smoke and soot damage arising out of one of the events in 2.3.1 to 2.3.8 is
covered.

Beyond that, damage is covered where smoke or soot directly damages or destroys
insured property, on condition that the smoke or soot escaped suddenly, and
contrary to intended operation, from a firing, heating, cooking or drying
installation situated on the insured site. Indemnity for this extension is
capped at [amount].

Not covered is damage arising from the gradual action of smoke or soot -
long-term surface soiling of the fogging type, for instance.

2.3.10 Damage excluded within the fire group
Not covered:
  (a) damage caused by earthquake, irrespective of any contributing causes;
  (b) damage to internal combustion engines caused by the explosions occurring
      inside the machine's combustion chamber, and damage arising at the
      switching elements of electrical switches through the gas pressure
      occurring inside them. Cover does exist, however, where such damage is
      the consequence of an insured fire event under 2.3.1.

2.4 Escape of water defined

2.4.1 The three headings
The escape of water peril covers three things: escape of water damage; fracture
damage to pipework inside buildings; and fracture damage to pipework outside
buildings.

2.4.2 Escape of water damage
Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended purpose
from:
  (a) pipes of the water supply, whether supply or drainage lines, or hoses
      connected to them;
  (b) other installations connected to those pipes or hoses, or the
      water-carrying parts of such installations;
  (c) heating or air-conditioning systems;
  (d) water-based extinguishing or sprinkler systems;
  (e) water beds or aquaria.

Operating fluids from heating or air-conditioning systems, and steam, also
count as escaping water. Fluids intended for the generation of energy do not.

Damage is also covered where it is caused by water that emerged, contrary to
its intended purpose, from rainwater drainage pipes running inside the
building. For this extension the exclusion of damage caused by precipitation
(see 3.3(c)) does not apply.

2.4.3 Fracture damage to pipework inside buildings
Covered inside buildings:

  (a) frost-related and other fracture damage to pipes of
        - the water supply, whether supply or drainage lines, and the gas
          supply, or hoses connected to them;
        - heating or air-conditioning systems;
        - water-based extinguishing or sprinkler systems;
        - rainwater drainage.
      This presupposes that the pipes concerned are not a structural component
      of a boiler, a water heater or a comparable installation.

  (b) frost-related fracture damage to the following installations:
        - bath and shower fittings, washbasins, lavatories, taps and valves
          together with their connection hoses;
        - radiators, boilers, water heaters and comparable parts of heating or
          air-conditioning systems.

The whole structural body of the building, including the floor slab, counts as
"inside the building". Pipes of a solar heating installation on the roof count
as pipes inside the building. Unless something else has been agreed, pipes and
installations beneath the floor slab are not insured, whether load-bearing or
not.

2.4.4 Fracture damage to pipework outside buildings
Covered outside buildings: frost-related and other fracture damage to supply
pipes of the water supply, or to pipes of heating or air-conditioning systems,
in each case insofar as the policyholder bears the risk for those pipes and
insofar as they either
  (a) serve the supply of insured buildings or installations, or
  (b) are situated on the insured site.

Indemnity for fracture damage to supply pipes that do not serve the supply of
insured buildings or installations is limited per insured event to the amount
agreed for that purpose.

Indemnity for fracture damage to supply pipes that are not situated on the
insured site is limited per insured event to the amount agreed for that
purpose.

2.5 Natural hazards defined

2.5.1 Storm
Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength, expressed as a defined
minimum sustained wind speed.

Where the wind strength at the loss location cannot be established, storm is
presumed if the policyholder demonstrates either of the following:
  (a) in the vicinity of the insured site the air movement caused damage to
      buildings that were in sound condition, or to other property of
      comparable resistance; or
  (b) given the sound condition of the insured building - or of the building in
      which the insured property was located - the damage can only have arisen
      through storm. This applies equally to buildings structurally joined to
      the insured building.

2.5.2 Hail
Hail means solid precipitation in the form of grains of ice.

2.5.3 Which storm and hail events are covered
Only damage arising in one of the following ways is covered:
  (a) storm or hail acts directly on insured property, or on buildings in which
      insured property is located; consequential damage to insured property
      arising from this is covered;
  (b) storm or hail acts directly on buildings structurally joined to the
      insured building;
  (c) storm or hail acts directly on buildings structurally joined to buildings
      in which insured property is located;
  (d) storm or hail throws building parts, trees or other objects onto insured
      property, or onto buildings in which insured property is located;
      consequential damage to insured property arising from this is covered;
  (e) storm or hail throws building parts, trees or other objects onto
      buildings structurally joined to the insured building;
  (f) storm or hail throws building parts, trees or other objects onto
      buildings structurally joined to buildings in which insured property is
      located.

2.5.4 The further natural hazards

Flood
Flood means the inundation of the ground and soil of the insured site, or of
directly adjoining land, roads, footpaths or cycle paths, with substantial
quantities of surface water. It counts only where the inundation was caused by
  (a) the overflow of surface waters, standing or flowing,
  (b) precipitation, or
  (c) the emergence of groundwater at the surface as a consequence of (a) or
      (b).

Backing-up of water
Backing-up is present where water enters the building from the building's own
drainage pipes or from installations connected to them. It counts only where
the backing-up was caused by the overflow of surface waters, standing or
flowing, or by precipitation.

Earthquake
Earthquake means a naturally caused tremor of the ground triggered by
geophysical processes within the earth's interior.

Earthquake is presumed if the policyholder demonstrates either of the
following:
  (a) in the vicinity of the insured location the naturally caused ground
      tremor caused damage to buildings that were in sound condition, or to
      other property of comparable resistance; or
  (b) given the sound condition of the insured property, the damage can only
      have arisen through an earthquake.

Ground subsidence
A naturally caused sinking of the ground above naturally formed cavities.

Landslip
A naturally caused sliding or falling away of masses of earth or rock.

Snow load
The effect of the weight of masses of snow or ice. Snow or ice masses sliding
off roofs also count as snow load.

Avalanche
Masses of snow or ice descending a mountain slope.

Volcanic eruption
A sudden release of pressure on the rupturing of the earth's crust, accompanied
by flows of lava, eruptions of ash, or the escape of other materials and gases.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing
causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered. This applies
irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.2 Exclusions within the fire group

See 2.3.10.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

Damage caused by the following is not covered, irrespective of any contributing
causes except where such causes are named below:
  (a) splash water or cleaning water;
  (b) dry rot and house-rot fungi of every kind;
  (c) groundwater, standing or flowing surface water, flood, precipitation, or
      a backing-up of water brought about by any of these causes;
  (d) earthquake, snow load, avalanche, volcanic eruption;
  (e) ground subsidence or landslip - unless escaping water within the meaning
      of 2.4.2 caused the subsidence or the landslip;
  (f) fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning; explosion;
      deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft; vehicle impact;
      scorching; smoke and soot damage;
  (g) the opening of sprinklers or the operation of sprinkler nozzles on
      account of a fire, on account of pressure testing, or on account of
      alteration or repair work to the insured building or to the extinguishing
      or sprinkler system;
  (h) storm, hail.

Damage to buildings or parts of buildings that are not ready for occupation is
not covered. The same applies to property located in such buildings or parts of
buildings.

3.4 Exclusions within the natural hazards

Damage caused by the following is not covered, irrespective of any contributing
causes except where such causes are named below:
  (a) storm surge;
  (b) the penetration of rain, hail, snow or dirt through windows, external
      doors or other openings that were not properly closed. This exclusion
      does not apply where those openings were created by storm or hail and
      constitute damage to the building;
  (c) groundwater, except insofar as it emerged at the surface as a result of
      precipitation or of the overflow of surface waters;
  (d) fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning; explosion;
      deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft; vehicle impact;
      scorching; smoke and soot damage. This exclusion does not apply insofar
      as those perils were triggered by an insured earthquake;
  (e) drought or desiccation.

Damage to buildings and parts of buildings that are not ready for occupation,
and to property located within them, is not covered. Damage to shop windows and
display windows is likewise not covered.

3.5 Items the insured event did not damage, and additions to the building

Not covered, irrespective of the occasion on which the work is carried out:
  (a) the supply and putting in place of new equipment within the meaning of
      1.3, and every element belonging to it;
  (b) the renewal, upgrading or supplementing of an installation that the
      insured event did not damage;
  (c) the extension or improvement of the technical equipment, the output, the
      capacity or the fitting-out of the building beyond the standard in place
      immediately before the insured event;
  (d) work directed at the comfort, convenience or appearance of a room, as
      distinct from making good the damage the insured event caused;
  (e) every ancillary charge within the meaning of 1.3 attributable to an item
      or a measure falling under (a) to (d).

This exclusion applies whether the work is carried out at the same time as
covered work, in the course of it, in the same room, by the same undertaking,
under the same commission, or on the same account; and whether or not it is
described as necessary, sensible, recommended or overdue.

Where covered and non-covered items appear on one account, the presence of the
covered items does not carry the others; each is assessed on its own merits
(9.5).

3.6 Work beyond the affected items, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those items of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event is not covered. Outlay that does not constitute a
repair or replacement cost is not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is
governed by 7.1.5 to 7.1.13.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises:
  (a) the buildings identified in the schedule;
  (b) their building components, including the technical installations forming
      part of them;
  (c) their building accessories;
  (d) terraces on the insured site that directly adjoin the building;
  (e) further site installations.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground. They must be capable of
affording protection against external influences and, for the purposes of these
conditions, must be intended for predominantly residential use.

Where the insured property is a self-contained dwelling within such a building,
these conditions apply to that dwelling and to those parts of the building that
constitute the policyholder's separate property, together with the
policyholder's share in the common parts.

4.2.2 Building components
Building components are items incorporated into a building that have lost their
independence through their firm connection with it. Fitted furniture and fitted
kitchens fall within this category where they were made individually for the
building and adapted to it with substantial installation effort. Add-on
furniture and add-on kitchens that are series-produced do not.

Also counting as building components are the fitting-out elements of the
dwelling: floor coverings together with their bedding, adhesive, underlay,
insulating and levelling layers; wall and ceiling finishes; interior doors; and
fixed trim, beading and comparable edging elements.

4.2.3 Technical installations of the building
The installations serving the building - heating, ventilation, climate control,
sanitary and electrical plant - are building components where they are firmly
connected with the building within the meaning of 1.3 and were in place
immediately before the insured event. Their fixed supports, brackets, consoles,
frames, mountings, ducting and connection elements form part of them.

The following are not building components:
  (a) an item that is not firmly connected - one that stands, rests, plugs in or
      is set down and can be taken elsewhere and used there without work on the
      fabric of the building. Its weight, its price, its designation as part of
      a system, and its being supplied together with fixed elements or with
      loose control devices do not alter this;
  (b) the loose, handheld or portable accessories supplied with an installation.

4.2.4 Building accessories
Building accessories are movable items located inside the building or attached
to its exterior. They must serve the upkeep of the insured building or its
predominant intended purpose.

4.2.5 Terraces
Terraces are paved surfaces intended for occupation in the open air.

4.2.6 Further site installations
Further site installations means the items firmly connected with the ground and
soil of the insured site that are specified for that purpose in the schedule.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) photovoltaic installations and their components - solar modules, mounting
      frames, fastening elements, inverters, module optimisers and the cabling.
      This extends to an electricity storage installation permanently connected
      to the photovoltaic installation and serving the supply of the building;
  (b) all items subsequently incorporated into the building by a tenant or by a
      condominium owner where that person both
        - procured or took the items over at their own expense, and
        - bears the risk for them.
      Where items are merely exchanged, the newly incorporated items are
      insured. Any different arrangement as to who bears the risk must be
      evidenced by the policyholder;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs. Costs of restoring
      electronically stored data and programs are covered only where this has
      been additionally agreed in the contract;
  (d) movable technical appliances and equipment of the household that are not
      firmly connected with the building within the meaning of 1.3, together
      with the elements and ancillary charges belonging to them. Such property
      is the subject matter of a separate class of insurance;
  (e) new equipment within the meaning of 1.3, together with the elements
      belonging to it and the ancillary charges attributable to it.

4.4 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel or parcels on which
the insured building stands. Where several buildings stand on one parcel, the
insured location is that part of the parcel which, by fencing or other
demarcation, belongs exclusively to the insured building or buildings.

4.5 Condominium and part-ownership units

4.5.1 Where the contract is with an association of condominium owners: if the
insurer is wholly or partly released from liability on account of the conduct of
individual condominium owners, it remains obliged to pay the remaining owners.
This applies to their separate property and to their shares in the common
property.

4.5.2 The co-ownership share of the owner against whom the insurer is wholly or
partly released is not indemnified, or is indemnified only in part.

The remaining condominium owners may nevertheless claim indemnity for that
co-ownership share. This presupposes that the additional indemnity is applied to
reinstating the common property. The condominium owner against whom the insurer
is wholly or partly released must reimburse the insurer for that additional
indemnity.

4.5.3 The two provisions above apply correspondingly to buildings insurance for
part-ownership units.

4.6 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually. They may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set
out in the schedule. Where one event damages several installations, the
deductible is applied once for that event. A deductible is applied only to an
indemnity that is otherwise payable; it does not create cover for an item that is
excluded.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) debris removal and demolition costs;
  (b) costs of moving and protecting property;
  (c) costs of lost water, gas and heating oil, and of electricity lost from
      storage installations;
  (d) hotel costs.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it. The
list is exhaustive. A cost that does not fall under one of these heads, and is
not a repair or replacement cost under Part 7, is not indemnified however it is
described or invoiced.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Debris removal and demolition
Costs incurred in clearing away and demolishing insured property affected by the
insured event, and in disposing of an affected installation that a covered
replacement takes the place of. This includes the expense of removing rubble and
other remains of that property, transporting them to the nearest disposal site,
depositing them and destroying them.

It does not extend to the removal or disposal of property that the insured event
did not damage and that no covered replacement takes the place of - plant,
appliances or fittings taken out of the building on the same occasion for other
reasons, for instance - whether or not they are collected in the same operation
and whether or not the charge appears on the same account.

5.2.2 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting other property, reimbursable
where those measures serve to reinstate or replace insured property damaged by
the insured event.

case.description:
Electrical surge claim on the fixed building-services cover. A surge came through the mains and knocked out two of the fixed air conditioning units in the house, one in the living room and one in the kitchen. Both are wall-fixed, permanently wired units that serve the building.

Neither could be sensibly repaired, so both were replaced like-for-like. The living-room unit sits on a floor-standing console, the same kind of stand it had before. A technician shipped the replacement units in, fitted them and checked the wiring over.

Worth noting where each one is. The living-room unit is well clear of any cooking appliances. The kitchen unit is mounted on the kitchen wall, a couple of metres from the hob.
